thread.title: U.S. Stock Indexes Keep Making New Highs

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: U.S. Stock Indexes Keep Making New Highs
text:
U.S. stock indexes jumped to new highs in mixed volume as the Trump administration continued trade talks with Mexico and Canada. In the meantime, GDP for Q2 was stronger than expected and corporate profits jumped.
X The Nasdaq climbed 0.8%, while the S&P 500 added 0.5%. The Dow Jones industrial average and Russell 2000 each rose 0.3%.
Volume rose on the NYSE but fell on the Nasdaq.
Corporate after-tax profits in Q2 leapt 6.7% vs. the year ago quarter, and the second reading on second quarter GDP came in at 4.2%, topping the consensus estimate of 4%.

Some Republicans were skeptical.
Sen. Ben Sasse, R-Neb., said the deal is "empowering government bureaucrats rather than markets to determine the components in cars and other goods." Sen. Bob Corker, R-Tenn., said the deal was "more for optics" for the midterm elections "than it is reality."
Widely Held Issues Meanwhile, action was positive but restrained among widely held issues. Apple ( AAPL ) added 1% in brisk volume as it struck a new high. Microsoft ( MSFT ) popped 1.4% in below-average volume, and it too pegged a new high. Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) advanced 1.3% in average volume, scoring a new high.
